# 1 Samuel Chapter 26 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 165v–166r | **Source Image:** 1SA_026_page_001.jpg, 1SA_026_page_002.jpg

---

**1** The Ziphites went to Saul at Gibeah and said, "David is hiding on the hill of Hachilah, facing the wasteland."

**2** Saul set out with three thousand of Israel's best soldiers to search for David in the wilderness of Ziph.

**3** Saul made camp on the hill of Hachilah, beside the road facing the wasteland. David, who was living in the wilderness, saw that Saul had followed him there.

**4** David sent out scouts and confirmed that Saul had arrived.

**5** Then David went to the place where Saul had camped. He saw where Saul and Abner son of Ner, his army commander, were sleeping. Saul lay inside the circle of the camp, with his troops around him.

**6** David said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, "Who will go down into the camp with me to Saul?" Abishai said, "I'll go with you."

**7** So David and Abishai crept into the camp at night. There was Saul, sound asleep inside the encampment, with his spear stuck in the ground near his head. Abner and the soldiers lay sleeping around him.

**8** Abishai whispered to David, "God has delivered your enemy into your hands tonight. Let me pin him to the ground with one thrust of the spear — I won't need a second."

**9** But David said, "Don't kill him. Who can lay a hand on the LORD's anointed and be innocent?

**10** As surely as the LORD lives," David said, "the LORD Himself will deal with him. Either the LORD will strike him down, or his time will come and he'll die naturally, or he'll fall in battle.

**11** But the LORD forbid that I should touch His anointed. Just take the spear by his head and the water jug, and let's go."

**12** David took the spear and the water jug from beside Saul's head, and they slipped away. No one saw them, no one knew, no one woke up — because the LORD had put them all into a deep sleep.

**13** David crossed to the other side and stood on top of the hill, far away — a wide distance between them.

**14** He shouted to the troops and to Abner son of Ner: "Aren't you going to answer, Abner?" Abner called back, "Who are you, shouting at the king?"

**15** David said, "You're supposed to be a great warrior, aren't you? The best in Israel? Then why haven't you guarded your lord the king? Someone came into the camp to kill him!

**16** You've failed badly. As surely as the LORD lives, you all deserve to die for not protecting your lord, the LORD's anointed. Now look — where is the king's spear? Where is the water jug that was beside his head?"

**17** Saul recognized David's voice. "Is that you, my son David?" he asked. David answered, "It is, my lord the king."

**18** And he said, "Why is my lord still chasing his servant? What have I done? What crime am I guilty of?

**19** Please listen, my lord the king. If the LORD has turned you against me, then may He accept an offering from me. But if people are behind this, may they be cursed before the LORD! They have driven me from the LORD's land — as good as telling me, 'Go worship other gods.'

**20** Don't let my blood be spilled far from the LORD's presence. The king of Israel has come out to hunt a single flea — like chasing a partridge through the mountains."

**21** Saul said, "I have sinned. Come back, my son David. I will never harm you again, because you valued my life today. I have been a fool — I have made a terrible mistake."

**22** David answered, "Here is the king's spear. Send one of your men to come get it.

**23** The LORD repays everyone for their righteousness and faithfulness. He put you in my power today, but I refused to raise my hand against the LORD's anointed.

**24** Just as I valued your life today, may the LORD value my life and rescue me from every danger."

**25** Saul said to David, "May you be blessed, my son David. You will do great things and will surely triumph." Then David went on his way, and Saul returned home.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **26:8-11 — the second test**: This parallels the cave scene in chapter 24, but it's even more intimate. David stands over a sleeping, defenseless Saul in the dark. Abishai begs for permission to strike. David's refusal is not weakness — it's the deepest expression of his theology: God alone decides the fate of His anointed.

2. **26:12 — "the LORD had put them all into a deep sleep"**: The narrator doesn't leave this to chance. The Hebrew word tardemah — the same "deep sleep" God placed on Adam in Eden — is attributed directly to the LORD. David's infiltration is enabled by divine intervention.

3. **26:19 — exile theology**: David's argument reveals a profound belief: to be driven from the land of Israel is to be driven from the LORD's presence. "Go worship other gods" is not what anyone has literally said — it's what exile means in David's theology. Land and God are inseparable.

4. **26:21-25 — the final parting**: Saul's confession — "I have been a fool" — is heartbreaking in its honesty and futility. He sees the truth but cannot change. David and Saul never meet again after this exchange. Saul's last words to David are a blessing: "You will do great things." The tragedy is complete.

— PNEUMA
